definition: Zeroth is a platform for brain-inspired computing from Qualcomm.
details: It is based around a neural processing unit (NPU) AI accelerator chip and a software API to interact with the platform. It makes a form of machine learning known as deep learning available to mobile devices. It is used for image and sound processing, including speech recognition. The software operates locally rather than as a cloud application. Mobile chip maker Qualcomm announced in March 2015, that it would bundle the software with its next major mobile device chip, the Snapdragon 820 processor.

explainer.lead: Zeroth is Qualcomm's platform for brain-inspired computing built around an NPU AI accelerator chip and a software API. It brings deep learning to mobile devices locally rather than as a cloud application.

tiers.eli5: Like giving a phone its own small brain chip so it can recognize speech and images on the spot instead of asking a distant computer.
tiers.practitioner: Developers use the Zeroth API to run deep learning for image and sound processing, including speech recognition, directly on mobile hardware. The work stays on-device rather than in the cloud.
tiers.paperLevel: Zeroth is a platform comprising a neural processing unit (NPU) AI accelerator and a software API to interact with it, aimed at mobile deep learning.

explainer.example: Qualcomm announced in March 2015 that it would bundle Zeroth with its next major mobile chip, the Snapdragon 820 processor.
